headline: Multimodal learning models forecast resistance, cancer prognosis and drug response
label: Multimodal Machine Learning Prediction
summary: Heterogeneous clinical, genomic and sequence data are now being fused in single predictive models across resistance, oncology and ctDNA profiling.
synthesis: The dominant thread is fusion of heterogeneous inputs within a single predictive model. FARM combines structural, biophysical, protein language model, and AAIndex features to forecast resistance of uncertain M. tuberculosis mutations. Oncoformer applies a multimodal transformer to longitudinal EHR data and chest X-rays for pan-cancer diagnosis, staging and survival prediction. DrGee infers anticancer drug sensitivity from gene expression via gene essentiality, using DeepEEAA to predict IC50 values. A TabTransformer-CatBoost pipeline predicts K. pneumoniae meropenem resistance from gene presence-absence, with external AUROC 0.81 under clade-aware splits. ALFAssay estimates ctDNA fraction from cfDNA fragmentation features in shallow WGS. What is new is extension beyond conventional omics to longitudinal records, imaging and protein sequence representations. The items share no common dataset or benchmark, so comparative performance cannot be assessed.
